category_title: Low-attaining students lacking knowledge of mathematical representations like arrays
minimal_context: Riley is playing a multiplication game using playing cards to generate random numbers and needs to calculate nine multiplied by eight.
dialogue:
TUTOR: You drew a nine and an eight from the playing cards. Please calculate nine multiplied by eight.

STUDENT: This is good because it was something different and we get to use playing cards and do the maths questions. Let me try to figure out nine times eight...

TUTOR: Why don't you use an array to help you calculate it?

STUDENT: I don't know what an array is.

TUTOR: I will show you what it looks like. Now you try drawing an array of nine by eight to find the answer.

STUDENT: (Spends most of the time for the game drawing the array) Okay, I drew an array of nine by eight. The answer is 70.

options.A: Make sure not to give the student attention while he works on the multiplication game.
options.B: Allow the student to work at his own pace on the calculation and take breaks when desired.
options.C: Explain the multiplication concepts to the student in plain and simple terms, getting straight to the point.
options.D: Suggest a specific representation, such as an array, and model how to construct it for the student.
